question: What Is A REST API?
answerGeneral: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for designing networked applications. A REST API exposes resources via URLs and uses standard HTTP methods to interact with them: GET retrieves data, POST creates, PUT/PATCH updates, DELETE removes. REST is stateless — each request contains all information needed to process it, with no server-side session. Responses are typically JSON. REST is the dominant style for web APIs due to its simplicity, use of existing HTTP infrastructure, and broad language support.
answerGeneralTr: REST (Representational State Transfer), ağ uygulamaları tasarlamak için kullanılan bir mimari stildir. REST API, kaynakları URL'ler aracılığıyla açığa çıkarır ve onlarla etkileşim için standart HTTP metodlarını kullanır: GET veri alır, POST oluşturur, PUT/PATCH günceller, DELETE kaldırır. REST durumsuzdur — her istek, işlenmesi için gereken tüm bilgileri içerir, sunucu tarafında oturum yoktur. Yanıtlar genellikle JSON formatındadır. REST, basitliği, mevcut HTTP altyapısını kullanması ve geniş dil desteği nedeniyle web API'leri için baskın stildir.

## REST API

## What REST Means

REST is a set of architectural constraints, not a protocol. An API is RESTful when it follows these constraints:

```
1. Client-Server     → UI and data are separate concerns
2. Stateless         → No client state stored on server between requests
3. Cacheable         → Responses should indicate if they can be cached
4. Uniform Interface → Consistent resource URLs + HTTP methods
5. Layered System    → Client doesn't know if it talks to a load balancer, cache, etc.
```

## HTTP Methods → CRUD

```
GET    /users        → List all users
GET    /users/42     → Get user 42
POST   /users        → Create a new user
PUT    /users/42     → Replace user 42 entirely
PATCH  /users/42     → Partially update user 42
DELETE /users/42     → Delete user 42
```

## Statelessness in Practice

```typescript
// ❌ Stateful — server remembers session
app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  req.session.userId = user.id; // stored on server
});

// ✅ Stateless — token carries identity
app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  const token = jwt.sign({ userId: user.id }, SECRET);
  res.json({ token }); // client stores it, sends on every request
});
```

## REST Response Conventions

```
GET /users/42
  200 OK            → found
  404 Not Found     → doesn't exist

POST /users
  201 Created       → success, include Location header
  400 Bad Request   → validation failed

DELETE /users/42
  204 No Content    → deleted, no body
  404 Not Found     → already gone
```

question: What Is The Difference Between REST And GraphQL?
answerGeneral: REST and GraphQL are both API paradigms but with different philosophies. REST has multiple endpoints, each returning a fixed data shape — you often get too much data (over-fetching) or need multiple requests (under-fetching). GraphQL has a single endpoint where the client specifies exactly what fields it needs in a query. This eliminates over/under-fetching and is especially powerful for complex, nested data and when multiple clients (mobile, web) have different data needs. The trade-off: REST is simpler, has great HTTP caching, and is universally understood; GraphQL has a steeper learning curve, caching is harder, and errors always return 200 OK which can mask issues.
answerGeneralTr: REST ve GraphQL her ikisi de API paradigmalarıdır ancak farklı felsefelere sahiptir. REST'te birden fazla endpoint vardır ve her biri sabit bir veri şekli döndürür — genellikle çok fazla veri alırsınız (over-fetching) veya birden fazla istek yapmanız gerekir (under-fetching). GraphQL'de tek bir endpoint vardır ve istemci sorguda tam olarak hangi alanları istediğini belirtir. Bu, over/under-fetching'i ortadan kaldırır ve özellikle karmaşık, iç içe veriler ile birden fazla istemcinin (mobil, web) farklı veri ihtiyaçları olduğunda güçlüdür. Dezavantajları: REST daha basittir, harika HTTP önbellekleme sunar ve evrensel olarak anlaşılır; GraphQL'in öğrenme eğrisi daha dik, önbellekleme daha zordur ve hatalar her zaman 200 OK döndürür.

## REST vs GraphQL

## The Core Difference

```
REST: Server defines the shape
  GET /users/42  → { id, name, email, address, createdAt, ... }
  Client gets everything whether it needs it or not.

GraphQL: Client defines the shape
  query { user(id: 42) { name email } }
  Client gets exactly name and email — nothing more.
```

## Over-fetching and Under-fetching

```
REST Problem — Under-fetching
  Need to render a post with author name and first 3 comments:
  GET /posts/1          → gets post (no author name, no comments)
  GET /users/5          → gets author
  GET /posts/1/comments → gets all comments, take first 3
  = 3 round-trips

GraphQL Solution
  query {
    post(id: 1) {
      title
      author { name }
      comments(first: 3) { body }
    }
  }
  = 1 round-trip
```

## When To Choose Each

```
Choose REST when:
  - Simple CRUD APIs
  - Public APIs (wide tooling support)
  - HTTP caching is critical (CDN for GET endpoints)
  - Team is familiar with REST

Choose GraphQL when:
  - Multiple clients with different data needs (mobile vs web)
  - Deeply nested, relational data
  - Rapid iteration — add fields without versioning
  - BFF (Backend for Frontend) patterns
```

## GraphQL Gotchas

```
- Always returns 200 OK (check errors[] in response body)
- N+1 query problem — need DataLoader
- No native HTTP caching (need persisted queries or Apollo)
- Introspection can expose schema to attackers (disable in prod)
```

question: What Are HTTP Status Codes And Why Do They Matter?
answerGeneral: HTTP status codes are 3-digit numbers that tell the client what happened with their request. They're grouped by range: 1xx informational, 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx redirects (301 Moved Permanently, 304 Not Modified), 4xx client errors (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 429 Too Many Requests), 5xx server errors (500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable). Using the right status code matters because clients (browsers, mobile apps, API consumers) use them to decide how to handle responses — retrying on 503 but not 400, showing 'not found' on 404, redirecting on 401 to login.
answerGeneralTr: HTTP durum kodları, sunucunun isteğe ne olduğunu istemciye bildiren 3 haneli sayılardır. Aralığa göre gruplanırlar: 1xx bilgilendirici, 2xx başarı (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx yönlendirmeler (301 Moved Permanently, 304 Not Modified), 4xx istemci hataları (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 429 Too Many Requests), 5xx sunucu hataları (500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable). Doğru durum kodunu kullanmak önemlidir çünkü istemciler yanıtları nasıl işleyeceğine karar vermek için onları kullanır.

## HTTP Status Codes

## The Five Classes

```
1xx  Informational   → Request received, continuing process
2xx  Success         → Request successfully received, understood, accepted
3xx  Redirection     → Further action needed to complete the request
4xx  Client Error    → Request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled
5xx  Server Error    → Server failed to fulfil a valid request
```

## Most Important Status Codes

```
200 OK               → Standard success (GET, PUT, PATCH)
201 Created          → Resource created (POST) — include Location header
204 No Content       → Success, no body (DELETE)

301 Moved Permanently → Redirect, update your bookmarks
304 Not Modified      → Cache is still valid, no body sent

400 Bad Request       → Malformed syntax, invalid params
401 Unauthorized      → Not authenticated (send credentials)
403 Forbidden         → Authenticated but not authorised
404 Not Found         → Resource doesn't exist
409 Conflict          → State conflict (duplicate email, optimistic lock fail)
422 Unprocessable     → Validation error (body parses but fails rules)
429 Too Many Requests → Rate limited

500 Internal Server Error → Catch-all server failure
502 Bad Gateway           → Upstream service failed
503 Service Unavailable   → Down for maintenance or overloaded
```

## Common Mistakes

```typescript
// ❌ Always returning 200 with error in body (GraphQL style in REST)
res.status(200).json({ error: 'User not found' });

// ✅ Use the right code
res.status(404).json({ error: 'User not found' });

// ❌ Using 401 when you mean 403
// 401 = 'Who are you?' (unauthenticated)
// 403 = 'I know who you are, you just can't do this'

// ❌ Returning 500 for validation errors
// Validation failures are the client's fault → 400 or 422
```

question: What Is The Difference Between PUT And PATCH?
answerGeneral: PUT and PATCH both update resources but differ in scope. PUT replaces the entire resource — if you send a PUT with only a name field, all other fields become null or default. PATCH partially updates the resource — only the fields you include are changed. PUT is idempotent (calling it multiple times with the same data has the same result). PATCH is technically idempotent but implementations vary. In practice: use PUT when replacing a whole resource (like uploading a file), use PATCH for partial updates like changing a user's email without touching other fields.
answerGeneralTr: PUT ve PATCH her ikisi de kaynakları günceller ancak kapsam bakımından farklıdır. PUT tüm kaynağı değiştirir — yalnızca bir isim alanıyla PUT gönderirseniz, diğer tüm alanlar null veya varsayılan olur. PATCH kaynağı kısmen günceller — yalnızca dahil ettiğiniz alanlar değişir. PUT idempotent'tir (aynı veriyle birden fazla kez çağırmak aynı sonucu verir). PATCH teknik olarak idempotent'tir ancak uygulamalar farklılık gösterir. Pratikte: tüm bir kaynağı değiştirirken PUT kullanın, diğer alanları değiştirmeden bir kullanıcının e-postasını değiştirmek gibi kısmi güncellemeler için PATCH kullanın.

question: What Is API Versioning And Why Is It Needed?
answerGeneral: API versioning is a strategy to introduce breaking changes to an API without breaking existing clients. When you change a response shape, remove a field, or alter behaviour, clients built against the old API will break if they're not given time to migrate. Versioning creates a stable contract for each version. Common strategies: URL versioning (/v1/users, /v2/users) is the most visible and easiest to route; header versioning (Accept: application/vnd.api.v2+json) is cleaner but less discoverable; query param versioning (?version=2) is simplest but considered bad practice. Most public APIs (Stripe, GitHub) use URL versioning for clarity.
answerGeneralTr: API versiyonlaması, mevcut istemcileri bozmadan API'ye kırılgan değişiklikler getirmek için kullanılan bir stratejidir. Bir yanıt şeklini değiştirdiğinizde, bir alan kaldırdığınızda veya davranışı değiştirdiğinizde, eski API'ye göre oluşturulmuş istemciler geçiş için zaman verilmezse bozulur. Versiyonlama, her sürüm için stabil bir kontrat oluşturur. Yaygın stratejiler: URL versiyonlaması (/v1/users, /v2/users) en görünür ve yönlendirmesi en kolay olanıdır; header versiyonlaması (Accept: application/vnd.api.v2+json) daha temizdir ancak daha az keşfedilebilirdir; sorgu parametresi versiyonlaması (?version=2) en basit ancak kötü bir uygulama olarak değerlendirilir.
detailMd:
## API Versioning

## Why You Need It

```
Without versioning:
  v1 client calls GET /users/1 → expects { name, email }
  You rename 'name' to 'fullName' for v2
  v1 client breaks immediately

With versioning:
  GET /v1/users/1 → { name, email }     (still works)
  GET /v2/users/1 → { fullName, email } (new shape)
  Clients migrate when ready
```

## Versioning Strategies

```
1. URL Path (most common)
   GET /v1/users
   GET /v2/users
   ✅ Visible, easy to route, easy to test in browser
   ❌ Breaks REST purity (URL should identify resource, not version)

2. Request Header
   GET /users
   Accept: application/vnd.myapi.v2+json
   ✅ Clean URLs
   ❌ Hard to test, less discoverable

3. Query Parameter
   GET /users?version=2
   ✅ Simple
   ❌ Version is part of query, not identity; can conflict with caching

4. No Versioning (Additive Changes Only)
   Only add new fields, never remove or rename
   ✅ No migration burden
   ❌ Accumulates technical debt; can't fix mistakes cleanly
```

## Breaking vs Non-Breaking Changes

```
Breaking (requires new version):
  - Remove or rename a field
  - Change a field type (string → number)
  - Change HTTP method for an endpoint
  - Add a required request field

Non-breaking (safe to deploy):
  - Add a new optional field to response
  - Add a new endpoint
  - Add an optional request parameter
```

question: What Is CORS And How Do You Handle It?
answerGeneral: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a browser security mechanism that restricts web pages from making requests to a different domain than the one that served the page. When your frontend at app.com makes a fetch to api.com, the browser first sends a preflight OPTIONS request to check if the server allows it. The server must respond with the correct Access-Control headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, Access-Control-Allow-Headers) or the browser blocks the response. CORS is a browser enforcement — server-to-server calls are not affected. You handle it server-side by setting the correct headers, either explicitly or with a library like cors in Express.
answerGeneralTr: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing), web sayfalarının sayfayı sunan farklı bir alandan istek yapmasını kısıtlayan bir tarayıcı güvenlik mekanizmasıdır. app.com'daki frontend'iniz api.com'a bir fetch yaptığında, tarayıcı önce sunucunun buna izin verip vermediğini kontrol etmek için bir preflight OPTIONS isteği gönderir. Sunucu, doğru Access-Control başlıklarıyla yanıt vermelidir, aksi takdirde tarayıcı yanıtı engeller. CORS bir tarayıcı kısıtlamasıdır — sunucudan sunucuya çağrılar etkilenmez. Bunu sunucu tarafında ya açıkça ya da Express'teki cors gibi bir kütüphaneyle doğru başlıkları ayarlayarak ele alırsınız.

question: How Do You Authenticate API Requests?
answerGeneral: Common API authentication methods: API Keys are simple strings sent in a header (X-API-Key) or query param — easy but offer no expiry or fine-grained control. HTTP Basic Auth sends base64-encoded username:password in the Authorization header — only acceptable over HTTPS and mostly used for server-to-server. Bearer Tokens (JWT) are signed tokens issued after login, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. The server validates the signature without a DB lookup. OAuth 2.0 is the standard for third-party access (let Google login to my app) using short-lived access tokens and refresh tokens. For most web APIs, JWTs for authentication and OAuth for third-party delegation is the right combination.
answerGeneralTr: Yaygın API kimlik doğrulama yöntemleri: API Anahtarları, bir başlıkta (X-API-Key) veya sorgu parametresinde gönderilen basit dizelerdir — kolay ancak süre sonu veya ayrıntılı kontrol sunmaz. HTTP Basic Auth, Authorization başlığında base64 kodlanmış kullanıcı adı:şifre gönderir — yalnızca HTTPS üzerinde kabul edilebilir. Bearer Token'lar (JWT), girişten sonra verilen imzalı token'lardır. Sunucu, DB araması yapmadan imzayı doğrular. OAuth 2.0, üçüncü taraf erişimi için standarttır. Çoğu web API'si için, kimlik doğrulama için JWT ve üçüncü taraf delegasyonu için OAuth doğru kombinasyondur.
detailMd:
## API Authentication Methods

## 1. API Keys

```
X-API-Key: sk-abc123

✅ Simple to implement and use
✅ Good for server-to-server, webhooks
❌ No expiry, no user identity, hard to rotate
❌ If leaked, full access until manually revoked

Best for: internal services, B2B APIs, CLI tools
```

## 2. JWT Bearer Tokens

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9...

JWT = Header.Payload.Signature (all base64url)
Payload contains: { sub: 'user123', role: 'admin', exp: 1700000000 }

✅ Stateless — server verifies signature, no DB lookup
✅ Can embed claims (role, permissions)
✅ Short expiry (15min) limits blast radius if leaked
❌ Can't revoke before expiry without a denylist

Best for: user authentication in web/mobile apps
```

## 3. OAuth 2.0

```
User → App → 'Login with Google' → Google Auth Server
  ↓ issues authorization code
App exchanges code for access_token + refresh_token
App uses access_token for API calls

✅ User never gives your app their Google password
✅ Scoped access (read-only, specific resources)
✅ Refresh tokens for long-lived sessions
❌ Complex flow, many moving parts

Best for: third-party integrations, social login
```

## 4. Session Cookies

```
POST /login → Set-Cookie: session=xyz; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
Subsequent requests automatically send the cookie

✅ Works with HTML forms, no JS required
✅ HttpOnly prevents XSS access
❌ CSRF vulnerability (mitigate with SameSite + CSRF tokens)
❌ Stateful — server must look up session each request

Best for: traditional server-rendered web apps
```

question: What Is Rate Limiting And Why Should Every API Have It?
answerGeneral: Rate limiting restricts how many requests a client can make in a given time window. Without it, a single abusive client (or a bug in a client app with infinite retries) can overwhelm your server, degrade service for all users, and incur enormous infrastructure costs. Common strategies: Fixed Window (100 requests per minute, resets on the minute boundary), Sliding Window (smoother — counts requests in the rolling last 60 seconds), Token Bucket (accumulates tokens over time, allows bursts), and Leaky Bucket (output rate is constant regardless of input bursts). When rate limited, return 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header so clients know when to retry.
answerGeneralTr: Hız sınırlama, bir istemcinin belirli bir zaman diliminde yapabileceği istek sayısını kısıtlar. Olmadan, tek bir kötüye kullanan istemci (veya sonsuz yeniden denemeli bir istemci uygulamasındaki bir hata) sunucunuzu bunaltabilir, tüm kullanıcılar için hizmeti bozabilir ve büyük altyapı maliyetlerine yol açabilir. Yaygın stratejiler: Sabit Pencere (dakikada 100 istek), Kayan Pencere (daha akıcı), Token Bucket (zaman içinde token biriktirir, ani artışlara izin verir) ve Sızdıran Kova (çıkış hızı sabit). Hız sınırlandırıldığında, istemcilerin ne zaman yeniden deneyeceğini bilmesi için Retry-After başlığıyla 429 Too Many Requests döndürün.
detailMd:
## Rate Limiting

## Why It's Essential

```
Without rate limiting:
  - A bug causes client to retry in a tight loop → DDoS yourself
  - Competitor scrapes your entire product catalogue
  - One heavy user degrades experience for everyone
  - Unexpected viral traffic crashes the server
```

## Common Algorithms

```
Fixed Window
  100 req/min. Counter resets at :00 each minute.
  ❌ Allows burst of 200 at boundary: 100 at :59 + 100 at :00

Sliding Window
  Count requests in the rolling past 60 seconds.
  ✅ Smoother, no boundary spike
  ❌ More memory (store timestamps or use Redis sorted sets)

Token Bucket
  Bucket holds N tokens. Each request consumes one.
  Tokens refill at a steady rate.
  ✅ Allows controlled bursts (e.g. 20 burst, 5/s steady)

Leaky Bucket
  Requests enter a queue; processed at a fixed rate.
  ✅ Guarantees steady output rate
  ❌ Queued requests add latency
```

## Implementation (Next.js + Redis)

```typescript
import { Redis } from '@upstash/redis';

const redis = new Redis({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL!, token: process.env.REDIS_TOKEN! });

export async function rateLimit(ip: string, limit = 60, windowSec = 60) {
  const key = `rl:${ip}`;
  const count = await redis.incr(key);
  if (count === 1) await redis.expire(key, windowSec);
  return count > limit;
}

// In a route handler:
const ip = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') ?? 'anonymous';
if (await rateLimit(ip)) {
  return Response.json({ error: 'Rate limited' }, {
    status: 429,
    headers: { 'Retry-After': '60' },
  });
}
```

## Response Headers To Include

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 14
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000060
Retry-After: 46   (only on 429)
```

question: What Is The Difference Between Authentication And Authorisation?
answerGeneral: Authentication is proving who you are — verifying your identity (login with email/password, OAuth). Authorisation is determining what you're allowed to do — checking permissions after identity is established. A simple mnemonic: authentication = 'Who are you?', authorisation = 'What can you do?'. In HTTP terms: 401 Unauthorized means you're not authenticated (despite the confusing name), 403 Forbidden means you're authenticated but not authorised. Common authorisation models: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) assigns roles (admin, editor, viewer) to users; ABAC (Attribute-Based) makes decisions based on attributes of the user, resource, and environment.
answerGeneralTr: Kimlik doğrulama, kim olduğunuzu kanıtlamaktır — kimliğinizi doğrulamak (e-posta/şifre ile giriş, OAuth). Yetkilendirme, ne yapmaya izin verildiğinizi belirlemektir — kimlik doğrulandıktan sonra izinleri kontrol etmek. HTTP terimlerinde: 401 Unauthorized, kimlik doğrulanmadığınız anlamına gelir; 403 Forbidden, kimlik doğrulandığınız ancak yetkili olmadığınız anlamına gelir. Yaygın yetkilendirme modelleri: RBAC (Rol Tabanlı Erişim Kontrolü) kullanıcılara roller atar; ABAC (Özellik Tabanlı) kararları kullanıcı, kaynak ve ortamın özelliklerine göre verir.

question: How Do You Design Pagination For A REST API?
answerGeneral: There are three main pagination strategies. Offset pagination (?page=2&limit=20) is the most common — simple to implement and allows jumping to any page, but becomes slow on large datasets because the DB must scan all preceding rows. Cursor-based pagination uses an opaque cursor (usually the last row's ID or timestamp) — much more efficient for large or constantly-updated datasets because it uses indexed seeks. Keyset pagination is similar to cursor-based but uses actual column values. For public APIs and UIs with 'next/previous', cursor-based is preferred. Always return metadata: total count, next cursor or next page URL, so clients can render pagination controls.
answerGeneralTr: Üç ana sayfalama stratejisi vardır. Offset sayfalama (?page=2&limit=20) en yaygın olanıdır — uygulaması basit ve herhangi bir sayfaya atlamaya izin verir, ancak DB önceki tüm satırları taraması gerektiğinden büyük veri setlerinde yavaşlar. İmleç tabanlı sayfalama, opak bir imleç kullanır (genellikle son satırın ID'si veya zaman damgası) — büyük veya sürekli güncellenen veri setleri için çok daha verimlidir. Keyset sayfalama, imleç tabanlıya benzer ancak gerçek sütun değerlerini kullanır. İmleç tabanlı sayfalama tercih edilir.
